questions.scenario: A market-intelligence firm runs a multi-agent research system on the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator spawns eight regional search subagents in parallel and then a synthesis subagent. The pipeline runs as a Kubernetes Job on spot instances, and about 1 in 6 runs is preempted midway. Current recovery logic stores the coordinator's `session_id` in Redis and, when the Job restarts on a replacement pod, calls `query()` with `resume` set to that ID. Logs from the new pod show the session cannot be found, so the coordinator starts from zero and re-runs all eight regional searches, including the five that had already finished (each costs roughly $4 in tokens). The team wants recovery that skips completed regions and does not depend on which node the Job lands on. What is the most effective change?
options: Set `continue_conversation=True` on the restarted coordinator so the SDK picks up the most recent session without needing the stored ID.
Persist each subagent's findings as application state in durable storage with a manifest of completed regions, and inject it into a fresh coordinator prompt.
Raise `max_turns` on the coordinator and wrap `query()` in retry logic so a preempted run is retried with the same stored `session_id`.
Restart with `resume` plus `fork_session=True` so the new pod receives its own copy of the original session history to continue from.
questions.why_correct: Los archivos de sesión viven en el disco de la máquina que los creó: en un pod nuevo no existen. La doc recomienda no depender del resume: guardar los resultados (lo que ya terminó cada subagente) como estado de la aplicación y pasarlos al prompt de una sesión nueva. Con un manifest de regiones completas, el coordinador relanza solo las que faltan.

why_wrong.0: `continue_conversation` busca la sesión más reciente en el directorio de ESTA máquina; en el pod nuevo no hay ninguna, así que falla igual.
why_wrong.2: El problema no es un límite de turnos ni un error transitorio: el archivo de sesión no está en el host nuevo. Reintentar con el mismo ID da el mismo 'not found'.
why_wrong.3: Un fork copia el historial de una sesión existente; si el archivo de sesión no está en el host, no hay nada que copiar.

questions.rule: Pipeline en hosts efímeros: el estado que importa va a storage durable (manifest + resultados) y se inyecta en una sesión nueva; no confíes en el `resume` local.
questions.source_quote: Don't rely on session resume. Capture the results you need (analysis output, decisions, file diffs) as application state and pass them into a fresh session's prompt. This is often more robust than shipping transcript files around.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions. Sessions SDK: archivos de sesión locales al host; 'Don't rely on session resume' textual. continue/fork no sirven sin el archivo en el host nuevo. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A platform team built an internal dependency-audit service on the Claude Agent SDK (Python). Each request audits one monorepo package with `max_turns=40`, and many audits run concurrently from the same working directory on one server. About 25% of runs end with result subtype `error_max_turns` after the agent has already read 200–300 files. Today the error handler discards the run and starts a brand-new `query()` with `max_turns=80`, which repeats all the file reading and roughly doubles cost for those audits. Finance wants the retry to reuse the analysis already done. The service has the `ResultMessage` available in the error path. Which change best achieves this?
options: Catch the error result, keep its `session_id`, and call `query()` again with `resume` set to that ID and a higher `max_turns`.
Catch the error and call `query()` again with `continue_conversation=True` and a higher `max_turns` to pick up the interrupted audit.
Capture `session_id` only on `success` results, then resume failed audits from the most recent successful session for that package.
Split each audit into one `query()` per subdirectory with `max_turns=40`, so no single run can reach the turn limit again.
questions.why_correct: La doc lista justamente este caso: si la corrida terminó con `error_max_turns`, se reanuda esa sesión con un límite más alto. El `session_id` viene en el result message aunque sea un error, y como hay muchas auditorías en paralelo, hay que reanudar por ID específico.

why_wrong.1: `continue_conversation` toma la sesión más reciente del directorio; con auditorías concurrentes en el mismo directorio puede reanudar la de otro paquete. Para varias sesiones la doc pide `resume` con el ID.
why_wrong.2: El `session_id` está en todos los result messages, éxito o error. Reanudar una sesión exitosa vieja no recupera el trabajo de la corrida que falló.
why_wrong.3: Cambia el diseño y puede ayudar a futuro, pero descarta lo ya leído en la corrida fallida: vuelve a repetir el trabajo que Finanzas quiere evitar.

questions.rule: `error_max_turns` / `error_max_budget_usd` → `resume` con el `session_id` de ese resultado y un límite más alto. Varias sesiones a la vez → ID, nunca `continue`.
questions.source_quote: Recover from a limit. The first run ended with `error_max_turns` or `error_max_budget_usd` (see Handle the result); resume with a higher limit.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions. Sessions SDK: 'Recover from a limit' textual; continue toma la más reciente del directorio (choque con concurrencia); session_id presente en todo result. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A fintech's platform team uses an Agent SDK agent to plan a refactor of its payments service. Session A holds two hours of analysis: call graphs, invariants, and risk notes. The architect wants to explore two competing strategies from that same baseline at the same time, event sourcing and a transactional outbox, with each agent editing code and running tests. The team launched two `query()` calls with `resume=A` and `fork_session=True`, both using the same repository checkout as `cwd`. The forks have separate session IDs and their conversations look independent, yet the outbox agent's test runs fail on files containing event-sourcing changes it never made, and its diffs mix both designs. What is the root cause and fix?
options: Forking copies history only partially; resume session A once without forking and give each strategy its own instructions in separate prompts.
Enable file checkpointing on the outbox fork and call `rewind_files()` before it starts, so it always begins from a clean working tree.
Forks branch conversation history, not the filesystem; give each fork its own working copy, such as a separate git worktree used as its `cwd`.
Fork the original session A as well, so neither strategy writes into A's history and the baseline files stay protected from both forks.
questions.why_correct: El fork bifurca la conversación, no el disco. Si los dos forks trabajan en el mismo directorio, las ediciones de uno son reales y visibles para el otro. Para explorar en paralelo hay que aislar también los archivos, por ejemplo con un worktree por fork.

why_wrong.0: El fork sí copia el historial completo. Reanudar A dos veces sin fork mezcla las dos conversaciones y no arregla el problema de los archivos compartidos.
why_wrong.1: Los checkpoints quedan atados a la sesión que los creó y solo siguen las ediciones de esa sesión. No deshacen lo que el otro fork sigue escribiendo en paralelo.
why_wrong.3: Hacer fork de A no cambia nada en el disco: ninguna sesión, forkeada o no, aísla el filesystem.

questions.rule: `fork_session` = rama de conversación, no de archivos. Agentes en paralelo que editan → un directorio de trabajo por agente.
questions.source_quote: Forking branches the conversation history, not the filesystem. If a forked agent edits files, those changes are real and visible to any session working in the same directory.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions. Sessions SDK: 'Forking branches the conversation history, not the filesystem' textual; checkpoints no aíslan forks paralelos. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A developer on Windows 11 uses Claude Code in PowerShell to run a three-step data migration for a SaaS product: (1) backfill a new `tenant_region` column, (2) verify counts, (3) drop the legacy column. Claude launched `npm run migrate:backfill` through the PowerShell tool; the backfill normally takes about 40 minutes. Twenty minutes in, Windows Update rebooted the laptop. The developer reopened the session with `claude --resume region-migration`. In the transcript, the backfill tool call shows no result, and Claude now says: 'The backfill step was started earlier, so next I'll verify counts and drop the legacy column.' Dropping the column early would lose data for tenants that weren't backfilled. What should the developer do first?
options: Run `claude --continue --fork-session` so the forked process starts clean and replays the pending backfill call automatically.
Let Claude proceed with verification, because a resumed session reruns interrupted tool calls before the next turn starts.
Use `/rewind` to restore the checkpoint from before the backfill, then let Claude continue with the verification step.
Tell Claude the interrupted command was not rerun on resume, and have it check the backfill state in the database before continuing.
questions.why_correct: Al reanudar, una tool que estaba corriendo cuando se cayó el proceso no se vuelve a ejecutar. El backfill quedó a medias y Claude no tiene su resultado. Lo primero es decírselo y confirmar el estado real en la base antes de cualquier paso destructivo.

why_wrong.0: Un fork copia la conversación, pero no vuelve a correr las tool calls interrumpidas: el backfill sigue sin terminar.
why_wrong.1: Es justo al revés: la doc dice que una tool interrumpida por un crash no se re-ejecuta al reanudar.
why_wrong.2: Los checkpoints de Claude Code siguen ediciones de archivos, no el estado de una base de datos. Rebobinar no te dice cuántas filas se rellenaron.

questions.rule: Resume después de un crash: lo que estaba corriendo NO se re-ejecuta. Verificá el estado real antes de seguir.
questions.source_quote: Interrupted tool calls: a tool that was still running when the previous process ended, for example in a crash, doesn't get rerun when you resume.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions. Sessions (Claude Code): tool interrumpida no se re-ejecuta al reanudar, textual; checkpoints solo cubren ediciones de archivos. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A developer-productivity team at a logistics company uses Claude Code to map a legacy billing module (about 140 files) before a rewrite. The lead asks Claude to 'explore the billing module and list every place that computes tax', and Claude delegates to the built-in Explore agent, which returns a good summary. An hour later, in the same session, she asks Claude to 'continue that exploration and now trace where the computed tax is persisted'. Claude launches a brand-new exploration that re-reads most of the 140 files, taking another 12 minutes. The team runs this explore-then-follow-up pattern several times a day and wants follow-ups to continue the earlier subagent's work instead of starting over. What should they change?
options: Ask Claude to invoke Explore at the `very thorough` level so the first pass covers the module completely and no follow-up is needed.
Define a custom read-only exploration subagent, or use `general-purpose`, so Claude gets an agent ID it can resume for follow-ups.
Quit and run `claude --resume` on the same session, since subagent transcripts persist and Explore is then resumed automatically.
Ask Explore to return its complete raw file listing and excerpts so the main conversation keeps everything for later follow-ups.
questions.why_correct: Explore y Plan pueden terminar sin darle a Claude un ID para reanudarlos, así que cada follow-up arranca de cero. Para trabajo que vas a continuar, la doc dice que uses `general-purpose` o un subagente propio: Claude recibe el agent ID y lo reanuda con todo su historial.

why_wrong.0: Más profundidad en la primera pasada no evita que cada pregunta nueva necesite seguir trabajando; Explore sigue siendo de una sola pasada.
why_wrong.2: Reanudar la sesión principal no le da a Claude un ID de Explore para retomarlo: el problema es el tipo de subagente, no el proceso.
why_wrong.3: Traer todo el material crudo al hilo principal es justo lo que el subagente evita: llena el contexto con contenido verboso.

questions.rule: ¿Vas a continuar el trabajo de un subagente? Usá `general-purpose` o uno propio (tienen agent ID); Explore y Plan son de una pasada.
questions.source_quote: For work you'll continue later, use `general-purpose` or a custom subagent. The built-in Explore and Plan agents can finish without giving Claude an ID to resume them with.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents. Sub-agents: Explore/Plan pueden terminar sin ID para reanudar; usar general-purpose o custom. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario:
An insurance company runs a claims-document pipeline on the TypeScript Agent SDK. Each claim is processed by one `query()` with `maxBudgetUsd` set, and many claims run concurrently in the same working directory. The handler looks like this:

`if (message.type === "result" && message.subtype === "success") { await db.saveSessionId(claimId, message.session_id); }`

About 9% of runs end with `error_max_budget_usd` after most of the documents are analyzed. Operations wants to resume exactly those runs with a larger budget, but the database has no session IDs for them, so they are re-run from scratch. Re-running costs about $2,100 a week. What change lets operations resume the failed runs?
options: Pass `continue: true` with a larger budget when re-running a failed claim, so the SDK finds the interrupted session without a stored ID.
Call `listSessions()` after each failure and resume the most recently modified session in the working directory with a larger budget.
Save `session_id` from every result message before checking `subtype`, then resume a failed claim by that ID with a larger budget.
Generate a UUID per claim and pass it as `resume` on the first run, so the retry can reuse the same predictable session identifier.
questions.why_correct: El `session_id` viene en todos los result messages, sea éxito o error. El handler lo descarta justo en las corridas que interesan. Guardándolo siempre, operaciones puede reanudar cada reclamo fallido por su ID con más presupuesto.

why_wrong.0: `continue: true` toma la sesión más reciente del directorio. Con muchos reclamos en paralelo, puede reanudar el de otro cliente.
why_wrong.1: Con concurrencia, 'la más reciente' es una carrera: puede ser otra corrida. Además es frágil frente a lo que la doc ya resuelve: el ID está en el resultado.
why_wrong.3: `resume` sirve para retomar una sesión que ya existe, no para elegir el ID de una nueva. El ID real se lee del result message.

questions.rule: Guardá el `session_id` de TODO result message (también los de error): sin él no hay `resume`.
questions.source_quote: Read it from the `session_id` field on the result message (`ResultMessage` in Python, `SDKResultMessage` in TypeScript), which is present on every result regardless of success or error.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions. Sessions SDK: session_id en todo result message sin importar éxito o error, textual; continue/listSessions no resuelven con concurrencia. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A code-generation team built a codemod pipeline on the Python Agent SDK with `enable_file_checkpointing=True`. The main agent plans the migration and delegates the actual file changes to a `refactor-worker` subagent that uses the Edit tool on about 40 files. When a run produces a broken build, the pipeline resumes the same session by ID and calls `rewind_files()` with the checkpoint taken before the codemod started. After the rewind, `git status` still shows 37 of the 40 files modified; only the three files the main agent had edited itself were restored. The conversation history is intact. The team needs a reliable way to undo a failed run. What explains the result, and what should they do?
options: Subagent edits aren't tracked by file checkpointing; revert those files with git, or have the tracked edits happen in the main conversation.
The rewind has to be issued from a forked session, otherwise the checkpoint history is overwritten while the files are being restored.
Resume the session from the message before the codemod started; resuming at an earlier point restores both the conversation and the files.
Enable checkpointing on the `refactor-worker` AgentDefinition as well, so its Edit calls are recorded in the same checkpoint stream.
questions.why_correct: El checkpointing no sigue las ediciones que hace un subagente (salvo una skill con `context: fork` en primer plano). El rewind solo revierte archivos que la conversación principal ya había editado; para el resto, la doc dice que uses git. Por eso volvieron solo 3 de 40.

why_wrong.1: No hace falta un fork para rebobinar; los checkpoints son de la sesión que los creó y se usan reanudando esa misma sesión.
why_wrong.2: Las sesiones guardan la conversación, no el filesystem: reanudar en un punto anterior no toca los archivos en disco.
why_wrong.3: `AgentDefinition` no tiene un campo de checkpointing; el límite es del mecanismo, no de la configuración del subagente.

questions.rule: Checkpointing = ediciones del hilo principal con Write/Edit. Subagentes y Bash quedan afuera → git.
questions.source_quote: Edits a subagent applies aren't tracked, except a skill with `context: fork` running in the foreground. A rewind reverts them only in files the main conversation had already edited; use git to revert the rest

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/file-checkpointing. File checkpointing: tabla de limitaciones, ediciones de subagentes no se trackean, usar git. Cita textual; AgentDefinition no tiene campo de checkpointing. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A team uses an Agent SDK harness to migrate 600 Jest test files to Vitest with no human in the loop. The work spans many context windows; when a window fills, the harness compacts and the agent continues. After the third window, logs show the agent re-migrating files it already converted (about 15% of its edits are no-ops) and, twice, deleting a failing test 'to make the suite green'. The only state carried between windows is the compaction summary. The team cannot add human checkpoints and wants each new window to know exactly which files are done, which tests pass, and what was decided. What is the most effective change?
options: Move to a 1M-token context model variant so the whole migration fits in one window and compaction never needs to run.
Have the agent append a narrative paragraph about each migrated file to CLAUDE.md, so every new window loads the history.
Keep per-file and per-test status in a JSON file, freeform notes in `progress.txt`, commit to git, and read them at each window start.
Lower the compaction threshold so summaries happen more often and each one carries a shorter, more precise list of migrated files.
questions.why_correct: Para tareas de varias ventanas, la doc recomienda guardar el estado estructurado (resultados de tests, estado de tareas) en JSON, notas libres en texto y usar git como log y checkpoint. Cada ventana nueva arranca leyendo esos archivos, no un resumen que pierde detalles.

why_wrong.0: Una ventana más grande no garantiza que entren 600 archivos ni evita la degradación con más tokens; el estado sigue sin estar en un lugar confiable.
why_wrong.1: Prosa libre en CLAUDE.md no deja explícito qué está hecho y qué no, y además infla un archivo que se carga en cada sesión.
why_wrong.3: Compactar más seguido sigue dependiendo de resúmenes; el problema es justamente que el estado vive solo ahí.

questions.rule: Estado entre ventanas: JSON para lo estructurado, texto para notas, git para checkpoints. Nunca solo el resumen.
questions.source_quote: Use structured formats for state data: When tracking structured information (such as test results or task status), use JSON or other structured formats to make schema requirements explicit to Claude.

verification.notes: Correcta (opción C) acortada: era 159 caracteres contra 117–130 de los distractores y se delataba por largo. Respuesta y sentido sin cambios. Cita textual en la página, respaldo correcto.

questions.scenario: A company's CI pipeline (Linux runners) uses `claude -p` to review pull requests. Stage 1 analyzes the diff and stores `session_id` from `--output-format json`. Stages 2a (security) and 2b (performance) then run in parallel on the same runner, each with `claude -p "..." --resume "$SID"`, so both build on the stage-1 analysis. Developers can later resume a stage's conversation to ask follow-up questions about its findings. Since the parallel stages were introduced, developers report that when they resume the session, the security discussion is partly missing or interleaved with performance messages. The pipeline must keep 2a and 2b in parallel to stay under its 15-minute budget. What change fixes this?
options: Replace `--resume "$SID"` with `--continue` in both stages so each one picks up the most recent conversation on the runner.
Run 2a and 2b one after the other in a single job so only one process writes to the shared transcript at any time.
Use `--output-format stream-json` in one stage and `json` in the other, so their events carry different session identifiers.
Add `--fork-session` to each parallel `--resume` command and store the new session ID each stage reports for later follow-ups.
questions.why_correct: Si dos corridas `claude -p` reanudan la misma sesión a la vez, escriben en un solo transcript y después pueden faltar mensajes. La doc dice que agregues `--fork-session` a cada comando: cada etapa parte del análisis común con su propia sesión.

why_wrong.0: `--continue` también apunta a una conversación compartida (la más reciente) y no separa las dos etapas: sigue el mismo choque.
why_wrong.1: Funciona, pero rompe la restricción de presupuesto de tiempo: el pipeline necesita las dos etapas en paralelo.
why_wrong.2: El formato de salida no cambia a qué sesión se escribe; las dos siguen reanudando el mismo `$SID`.

questions.rule: Dos procesos reanudando la misma sesión a la vez → `--fork-session` en cada uno.
questions.source_quote: If you resume the same session in two terminals or two `claude -p` runs at the same time, both write to one transcript. When you resume that session later, messages from one of them can be missing. To keep both conversations, add `--fork-session` to each `claude` command.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions. Sessions (Claude Code): dos claude -p reanudando la misma sesión a la vez → --fork-session en cada uno. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A retailer's customer-support resolution agent runs on the Python Agent SDK inside a serverless function. Each customer message is handled by whichever instance is free; the function stores the conversation's `session_id` and calls `query()` with `resume` on the next message. Each invocation runs in a freshly created temporary directory. About 60% of follow-up messages fail to find the session and the agent greets the customer as if it were a new conversation. Compliance requires the agent to keep full transcript continuity (prior tool calls and refund decisions) across turns, so passing only a summary is not acceptable. Which design meets the requirement?
options: Attach a `session_store` adapter that mirrors transcripts to the company's database, and resume each turn from a `cwd` that matches the original run's.
Attach a `session_store` adapter, and keep giving each invocation its own unique temporary `cwd` so concurrent runs never collide on disk.
Switch follow-ups to `continue_conversation=True` so each instance resumes the most recent session without having to look up an ID.
Copy the transcript `.jsonl` into the function's local temp folder after each turn so the next invocation can find it before calling `resume`.
questions.why_correct: Los archivos de sesión son locales a la máquina. Para reanudar en otro host, la doc propone un adaptador `session_store` que replica los transcripts en tu backend. Ojo con el detalle: la clave de búsqueda sale del working directory, así que hay que reanudar con el mismo `cwd` que la corrida original.

why_wrong.1: Casi: el store es la pieza correcta, pero con un `cwd` distinto en cada invocación la clave de búsqueda no coincide y el resume sigue sin encontrar la sesión.
why_wrong.2: `continue_conversation` busca en el disco local de la instancia; en otra instancia no hay nada, y con varios clientes podría tomar la conversación equivocada.
why_wrong.3: La carpeta temporal es de esa instancia; la próxima invocación puede caer en otra máquina que no tiene el archivo.

questions.rule: Resume entre hosts → `session_store` + mismo `cwd` que la corrida original.
questions.source_quote: Attach a `sessionStore` / `session_store` adapter so the SDK mirrors transcripts to your own backend and another host can resume them. The store lookup key derives from the working directory, so resume from a `cwd` matching the original run's.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions. Sessions SDK, Resume across hosts: session_store + cwd igual al original. Cita textual; buen par casi-correcto con B. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.

questions.scenario: A consulting firm's multi-agent research system (TypeScript Agent SDK) has a coordinator that delegates literature searches to a custom `lit-search` subagent with `maxTurns: 25`. For broad topics, the subagent hits the limit and its output comes back marked as partial; the coordinator currently treats it as complete and synthesizes from it, so reports miss 20–30% of relevant papers. The team's first fix ran a second `query()` that asked Claude to 'continue the lit-search agent' using the agent ID captured from the Agent tool result, but the new run had no memory of the earlier search and started over. They want the search to continue where it stopped. What should they do?
options: Spawn a new `lit-search` subagent with `maxTurns: 60` for partial results, and pass the original topic so it re-runs the search with more room.
Detect the partial result, then call `query()` with `resume` set to the original session ID and ask Claude to continue that agent by its ID.
Raise the coordinator's own `maxTurns` so it has enough turns left to wait for the subagent and finish synthesis on a complete result.
Keep starting a fresh `query()`, but include the agent ID and the partial output in the prompt so the subagent reconstructs its history.
questions.why_correct: Cuando un subagente llega a `maxTurns`, su salida vuelve marcada como parcial y se puede reanudar. Pero cada `query()` arranca una sesión nueva: para acceder al transcript del subagente hay que reanudar la MISMA sesión y pedir que continúe ese agente por su ID. Eso faltaba en el primer intento.

why_wrong.0: Un subagente nuevo empieza de cero y repite toda la búsqueda; justo lo que se quiere evitar.
why_wrong.2: El límite que se alcanzó es el del subagente, no el del coordinador; darle más turnos al coordinador no completa la búsqueda.
why_wrong.3: Una sesión nueva no tiene el transcript del subagente; pegar la salida parcial no restaura sus tool calls ni su razonamiento.

questions.rule: Subagente parcial por `maxTurns` → `resume` de la misma sesión + continuar ese agente por ID.
questions.source_quote: Each `query()` call starts a new session by default, and you must resume the same session to access the subagent's transcript.

verification.notes: Revisada contra https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents. SDK subagents: maxTurns → salida parcial reanudable; cada query() es sesión nueva, hay que resume de la misma sesión + agent ID. Cita textual. Explicaciones en español, distractores no defendibles, largos parejos.
